brief: Agentic AI anticipation drove today's dispersion: big-tech beneficiaries were bid, pushing Nasdaq to a record high, while banks, seen as AI-disrupted, were battered, dragging the Dow to the day's biggest loss as the S&P finished flat. Goldman flagged negative AI spillover into financials, insurance and subscription businesses, compounding pressure from Fed rate-hike expectations and a flatter curve. Oil swung repeatedly on Iran talks: Brent fell as much as 4% below $100 after reports Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week, reversed on a Fars denial, dipped again on Saudi pipeline-restart hopes, then tanked to WTI down 3.5% after Trump called his Iran meeting very good, even as he separately said no deal is expected before the Midterms. Trump also floated a diesel export ban given price spikes from the Iran and Ukraine wars. Treasury yields ended flat despite falling inflation expectations, which Goldman called the weird bit since real-rate demand stayed high. Hyperscaler credit widened for a fourth straight day. Both long-only and hedge fund desks were net sellers despite subdued overall activity, and new lows have outpaced new highs for six sessions, a breadth pattern CNBC noted last seen in 1999 and 1929.
